t.E160a.agn: In 2012 EFSA could not set an ADI; it saw no safety concern as long as the amount taken in from additives and supplements does not exceed that from a normal diet (5–10 mg per day). For supplement use above 15 mg per day, there is evidence of a lung cancer risk, particularly in smokers.
t.E160a.body: Beta-carotene can be converted to vitamin A in the body.
t.E160a.eff.0.a: With supplement use above 15 mg per day
t.E160a.eff.0.t: There is evidence of a lung cancer risk
t.E160a.eff.1.w: In amounts equivalent to those from a normal diet
t.E160a.prod: Beta-carotene can be obtained by chemical synthesis, by extraction from plants, by fungal fermentation or from algae.
t.E160a.regx.0: No ADI could be set; no safety concern at normal dietary levels.
t.E160a.summary: Orange pigments (beta-carotene etc.) found in plants such as carrots; a precursor of vitamin A. Used in margarine, fruit juice and confectionery.
